title: Introduce soft-saturation fence and occupancy resampler for smoother burst handling
author: Maya Chen
ci_checks: ci/build: pass; ci/unit: pass; ci/integration: pass (canary perf unstable on first run, rerun fixed); ci/lint: pass; stress/loadbench: pass; e2e: pass
release_notes: Adds an opt-in soft saturation fence and an occupancy resampler to reduce noisy burst admissions and smooth autoscaler reactions. Backwards compatible behind a feature flag. Recommended: enable in canary pools before fleet-wide rollout.
body:
Context and motivation:
High-frequency microbursts against Dedicated pools occasionally produce sharp oscillations in autoscaler signals: transient occupancy spikes cause immediate admission tightness followed by aggressive decommit, which produces further instability and degraded tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing burst-hedging mechanisms are binary (allow/deny) or rely on single-window percentiles which overreact to short-lived bursts.

Goal:
Introduce a soft (graded) saturation fence that gates burst admissions by a continuously computed fence level and a low-cost occupancy resampler that provides a denoised, multi-window occupancy estimate. The combination should: (1) reduce reactionary autoscaler churn, (2) preserve burstability for short, safe probes, and (3) surface new telemetry for fine-grained SLO debugging.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new saturation_fence component into the admission path that computes a fence level in [0,1] combining per-pool occupancy, recent preemption events, and headroom forecasts. The fence is applied as a soft admission multiplier (0 -> block, 1 -> allow) rather than a hard reject.
- Implements an occupancy resampler service: periodically samples per-device occupancy at staggered offsets, aggregates into multiple EWMA windows (100ms, 1s, 10s) and produces a denoised occupancy vector used by autoscaler and admission.
- Introduces new telemetry: saturation_fence_level, occupancy_resample_rate, occupancy_ewma_{100ms,1s,10s}, and fence_decision_trace (sampled).
- Adds a feature flag saturation_fence.v1 (default off) with canary gating.
- Hooks the fence into the dedicated admission controller and the warm-pool balancing loop; autoscaler uses the resampler signal as a soft penalty term.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Soft vs hard: Soft multiplier reduces cliff-edge behavior and lets callers still probe at reduced concurrency; we believe this reduces painful oscillations seen in recent canaries.
- Sampling cost: resampler staggers sampling across devices and respects a configurable max_resample_rate. Typical added overhead measured ~0.3% CPU and 1-2% p95 tail memory for large pools.
- Consistency: fence computation is deterministic and lock-free for the fast path; we use an atomic slot swap to publish resampled vectors to prevent admission stalls.

Files changed (summary):
- pkg/autoscaler/resampler.go (new): occupancy resampling logic and multi-window EWMA aggregation.
- pkg/admission/saturation_fence.go (new): fence computation and admission multiplier wrapper.
- pkg/telemetry/metrics.go: metrics registration for new signals.
- cmd/dedicated/main.go: feature flag wiring and canary gating.
- docs/ops/saturation-fence.md: operator guide and rollout checklist.
- test/autoscaler/resampler_test.go: unit tests for resampler windows.
- test/integration/saturation_fence_e2e.go: deterministic e2e scenario.
- deploy/helm/values.yaml: feature flags default off.

Commits (high level):
- a1b2c3d: initial resampler implementation, basic EWMA windows and publish API
- b2c3d4e: saturation fence calculation and soft-admission wrapper
- c3d4e5f: metrics, tracing, and feature-flag integration
- d4e5f6g: unit and integration tests, docs, and canary rollout recipe
- e5f6g7h: performance tuning (reduced sample rate and memory allocations) and CI fixes

Testing and results:
- Unit tests: coverage added for EWMA math, edge cases (zero-length windows), and atomic publish.
- Integration: deterministic replay test simulating microbursts shows 42% reduction in autoscaler scale-in churning and 18% improvement in 99th-percentile tail latency under the same offered load.
- Loadbench: two canary pools run for 48 hours with feature enabled; overall CPU/memory overhead within expected margins.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (this PR).
2) Enable saturation_fence.v1 on a single low-traffic canary pool for 24h, monitor saturation_fence_level and occupancy_ewma signals.
3) If stable, expand to 10% of dedicated pools over 72h; observe autoscaler commit/reclaim rates and per-tenant latency.
4) Fleet-wide enable after 7d of positive canary signals.

Fallback and mitigation:
- Feature flag can be toggled off immediately to restore previous behavior.
- A kill-switch route added in the console to temporarily set the fence multiplier to 1.0 for a pool.

Related work and references:
- ENG-2157: investigate autoscaler oscillation during high burst churn
- ENG-2189: warm-pool prewarming improvements (this resampler feeds the warm-pool score)

Notes for reviewers (checklist):
- [x] Design: does the soft multiplier make sense for admission semantics?
- [x] Code: algorithm correctness and concurrency safety (look at atomic slot swap in resampler.go)
- [x] Telemetry: are metrics sufficiently descriptive and low-cardinality?
- [x] Tests: unit + integration scenarios included
- [x] Docs: ops guide and rollback procedure present

review_thread:
Ravi: This looks promising. Concern: global locks in resampler might contend under large fabric; can we avoid blocking the admission path?
Maya: Good catch — resampler publishes via atomic pointer swap; fast path only reads a single atomic slot (added comment and test).
Lina: Request to add more telemetry around why the fence adjusted (trace reason codes).
Maya: Added fence_decision_trace (sampled at 0.1%) and included reason tag (occupancy, preempt_count, forecast_delta).
Sergey: Observed a slight perf regression in one of the canaries on first run (p95 write latency). Is this expected?
Maya: Regression was due to unbounded goroutine creation in early prototype; fixed in e5f6g7h, reran canary and numbers are back to baseline.
Ravi (approve): Approving pending one nits file rename.
Maya: Addressed rename and pushed follow-up commit.
Merge: Squash merge after green CI and a short canary run.
metrics_telemetry_changes: New metrics: saturation_fence_level{pool}, occupancy_resample_rate{pool}, occupancy_ewma_100ms/1s/10s{pool}, fence_decision_trace (sampled). Updated exporters to include new metrics in prometheus scrape and OTLP pipeline.
operators_notes: Feature flag saturation_fence.v1 default off; enable in console under Dedicated -> Pools -> Feature Flags. Canary config provided at scripts/perf/loadbench/configs/saturation_fence_canary.toml. Watch: autoscaler.commit_rate, autoscaler.reclaim_rate, saturation_fence_level, occupancy_ewma_1s.
backout_steps: 1) Toggle saturation_fence.v1 to false in console or set env var SATURATION_FENCE_ENABLED=false for dedicated controller. 2) Restart dedicated controller if telemetry exporters stuck. 3) If necessary, rollback to previous release tag.
testing_summary: Unit tests added and passing. Integration e2e deterministic replay validates stability. Loadbench canary run for 48h; stress tests show reduced scale churn. CI unstable once due to linting import order; fixed in follow-up commit.
notes_for_release: Opt-in feature; recommend operators run 24h canary on low-traffic pool before wider rollout. No migrations needed. Metrics will appear after enabling.
